post.description:
Created lists can be used in scans, schedules, and other host lists

For example, with the following two lists created
{"name":"my_list_1","description":"some hosts","hosts":["1.2.3.4","2.3.4.5"],"host_count":2}
{"name":"my_list_2","description":"some other hosts","hosts":["3.4.5.6","4.5.6.7"],"host_count":2}

You can create a new list by referring to those lists by name.

'{"name":"my_full_list","description":"all my ssh hosts","hosts":["my_list_1", "my_list_2"]}'

Result:
{"name":"my_full_list","description":"all my ssh hosts","hosts":["1.2.3.4","2.3.4.5","3.4.5.6","4.5.6.7"],"host_count":4}

Links to the source lists are not maintained, so any later changes to the two source lists will not reflect in my_full_list.
You can update my_full_list after altering the 'my_list_1' and 'my_list_2' lists to reflect those changes

When a list is used in a Schedule, any updates to the list will be reflected in the schedule

RESTRICTIONS: 	Valid characters are: [a-zA-Z0-9_] host lists cannot contain hyphens, spaces will be replaced with underscore(_)

Created lists can be used in scans, schedules, and other port lists

For example, with the following two lists created
{"name":"ssh_basic_list","description":"common ssh ports","ports":"22,222,2222","port_count":3}
{"name":"ssh_alt_list","description":"extra ssh ports","ports":"223,2223,2323,22223","port_count":4}

You can create a new list by referring to those lists by name.

'{"name":"ssh_full_list","description":"all my ssh ports","ports":["ssh_basic_list", "ssh_alt_list"]}'

Result:
{"name":"ssh_full_list","description":"all my ssh ports","ports":"22,222-223,2222-2223,2323,22223","port_count":7}

Links to the source lists are not maintained, so any later changes to the two source lists will not reflect in ssh_full_list.
You can update ssh_full_list after altering the 'basic' and 'alt' lists to reflect those changes

When a list is used in a Schedule, any updates to the list will be reflected in the schedule

RESTRICTIONS: 	Valid characters are: [a-zA-Z0-9_] port lists cannot  or begin with 'top_' to avoid interfering with top_# lists.
No hyphens, spaces will be replaced with underscore(_)

define the parameters of your scan hosts: - "1.2.3.4/32" single (also ok without '/32') - "1.2.4.1/24" block - "1.2.5.1-1.2.5.19" range - "my_custom_list" custom user list ports: - "443" - "20-22" range - "top_10" top_# use any number up to 10,000 - "my_custom_list" custom user list fingerprint: - 0/omitted Just check if open - no fingerprinting attempts (fastest) - 1 Evaluate any banners sent upon connection - 2 Send probes to identify service if needed (possible multiple connections, slowest) Setting fingerprint to 1 or 2 doubles the request count of the job (hosts * ports * 2) checks: - true - false (default) Enabling our Checks system may extend the length of your jobs by multiple minutes, depending on what services or software are found, and what vulnerabilities exist for them. proto: - "tcp" (default) - "udp" collect: - "collect:{"ssh":["222","my_custom_ssh_port_list"],"rdp":["33389","my_custom_rdp_port_list"]} - collect bypasses fingerprinting, assumes any open port 222 is SSH, and attempts to collect domains currently limited to 20 per job domains can be provided with hosts/ports, paths, urls, and cves *adding paths or cves to your request means domains provided will not get whois/dns lookups as normal, just used for checks operations* - "somedomain.tld" - "www.somedomain.tld" - "some.subdomain.somedomain.tld" paths currently limited to 5 per job provided paths are appended to all host:port combinations, and domains, then used for http collection *adding paths to your request means you cannot include cves* *adding paths to your request means host/ports provided will not be scanned normally, just used for http collection* *adding paths to your request means domains provided will not get whois/dns lookups as normal, just used for http collection* - "/example/path" - "/admin/login.php" - "/something/here.html" urls currently limited to 20 per job can be provided with hosts/ports, domains, and paths *adding urls to your request means you cannot include cves* - "somedomain.tld/this/path" - "www.somedomain.tld/other/path.php" - "https://test.somedomain.tld/something/else/here" - "some.subdomain.somedomain.tld/something/else/here" cves currently limited to 5 per job can be provided with hosts+ports, domains *adding cves to your request means you cannot include urls or paths* *adding cves to your request means host:ports provided will not be scanned normally, just used as targets for checks operations* *adding cves to your request means domains provided will not get whois/dns lookups as normal, just used for checks operations* - "cve-2024-1234" - "CVE-2024-1235" callback: start_url: "mydomain.tld/hit/this/address/when/starting/$job_id" ('$job_id' (or $JOB_ID) will be replaced by your job_id) start_method: HTTP method to use POST(default) | GET - Post will post the job result data - "POST" (default) - "GET" success_url: "mydomain.tld/hit/this/address/when/complete/$job_id" ('$job_id' (or $JOB_ID) will be replaced by your job_id) success_method: HTTP method to use POST(default) | GET - Post will post the job result data - "POST" (default) - "GET" fail_url: "mydomain.tld/hit/this/address/upon/failure/$job_id" (not yet implemented) fail_method: HTTP method to use - "POST" (default) - "GET" email: we will email your account email address - true - false (default) summary_only: we will omit the results (useful if your webhook has a payload size limit) - true - false (default) We will populate the 'efflux-job-id' header with the job_id when we perform the callback

post.description: define how often and when you want your scan to occur frequency: '5m', '10m', '2h', '1d', '1w' valid intervals: 'm'(minute), 'h'(hour), 'd'(day)', 'w'(week) options: if interval = m (5,10,15,20,30) if interval = h (1,2,3,4,6,8,12) if interval = d/w (1) day: only if interval = w, (0[Sunday]-6[Saturday]) default 0 hour: only if interval = d/w, (0-23) default 0 all times GMT/UCT/ZULU hosts: same as scan request (custom lists supported) ports: same as scan request (top_# lists and custom lists supported) proto: "tcp"(default) or "udp" as with scans, request count = host count * port count max request counts depend on the frequency: "m": 1,000 per minute interval in the frequency (5m = 5,000) "h": 100,000 per hour interval in the frequency (2h = 200,000) "d": 1,000,000 per day "w": 10,000,000 per week callback: success_url: "mydomain.tld/hit/this/address/when/complete/$job_id" ('$job_id' (or $JOB_ID) will be replaced by your job_id) success_method: HTTP method to use POST(default) | GET - Post will post the job result data - "POST" (default) - "GET" email: we will email your account email address - true - false (default) summary_only: we will omit the results (useful if your webhook has a payload size limit) - true - false (default) Examples: '{"frequency":30m,"hosts":"1.2.3.4/28","ports":"top_1000"}' '{"frequency":1h,"hosts":"1.2.3.4/23","ports":"top_100"}' '{"frequency":6h,"hosts":"1.2.3.4/21","ports":"top_1000"}' '{"frequency":1d,"hour":16,"hosts":"1.2.3.4/16","ports":"top_1000"}' '{"frequency":1w,"day":2,"hour":12,"hosts":"1.2.3.4/16","ports":"top_1000"}'

cves_only.description: ensures only CVE checks run, as long as they meet other requirements.

min_severity.description: is the lowest severity check to run. Higher severities will also be run, up to max_severity, if included.

max_severity.description: is the highest severity check to run. Leave blank for no max.

include_ids.description: includes these check IDs even if they do not meet other requirements. Overrides cves_only and severity limits, but not exclude_ids.

exclude_ids.description: excludes these check IDs even if they meet other requirements. Overrides include_ids if id is both lists.

limit_to_ids.description: only includes the provided check IDs, as long as they meet other requirements. Overrides include/exclude.

exclude_targets.description: excludes the targets from any checks run.

limit_to_targets.description: only includes checks associated with these targets, as long as they meet other requirements. Overrides exclude_targets.
